findings.title: Float comparison tolerance can admit a retained head that fails the exact protection gate
findings.problem: Best qualification/ranking is derived from recorded history before replay. Retained CPU replay is checked only with math.isclose(rel_tol=1e-6, abs_tol=1e-7). The replayed metrics are never independently required to satisfy the exact protection gate or agree on qualification. A recorded reliable macro of0 can therefore pass against a negative actual replay macro, yet the predeclared reliable macro>=0 gate rejects that actual head.

independent_reproduction.actual_metrics_computed_with: The real action_metrics function on3949 synthetic states,2899reliable/800lost, one candidate per state and float64 IoUs.

findings.impact: A checkpoint can be labelled a best qualifying TRAIN head even though its independently recomputed protection statistic is negative. Numerical closeness must not relax a fixed decision boundary. Tolerance can also hide ordering differences in the floating ranking statistic.
findings.minimal_required_fix: For every replayed retained checkpoint and especially best.pth, evaluate the fixed qualification on replayed held metrics without gate tolerance and require it to agree with the recorded qualifies/selection result. Use replayed ranks for available retained comparisons and reject inconsistent selection rather than letting math.isclose imply qualification. Keep numeric tolerance only for non-decision reporting comparisons.
findings.required_regression: A retained/best checkpoint with actual reliable macro<0 but recorded0 must fail verification, even when abs(delta)<1e-7. Add a near-tie ranking case so tolerances cannot silently change the asserted ordering.

findings.title: latest.pth is accepted without strict state or metadata validation
findings.problem: Retained epoch files and best use verify_checkpoint, but latest only checks epoch/provenance/metrics and iterates the already verified epoch12 state keys with torch.equal. It does not require latest's exact state key set, finite extra values, original tensor dtypes, strict loading, selection_partition, test_eligible or total_parameters. A malformed latest therefore bypasses the checks applied to epoch12 even though latest is part of the accepted checkpoint set.

independent_reproduction.terminal_fixture_baseline: Accepted by the actual verify_completed with synthetic in-memory artifacts and explicit substituted admission/evaluation boundaries.
independent_reproduction.strict_load_of_that_latest: The actual E0RelativeIdentity.load_state_dict(..., strict=True) rejected its unexpected key.
independent_reproduction.wrong_latest_metadata: Changing latest test_eligible totrue, selection_partition to'test', and total_parameters to0 also still returned verified.

findings.impact: The verifier can certify a latest checkpoint that cannot be strictly reloaded into the declared model and whose selection/eligibility metadata contradicts the TRAIN contract.
findings.minimal_required_fix: Pass latest.pth through the same verify_checkpoint path for epoch12 and its expected metrics/provenance, then require exact equality with epoch12's validated net. This reuses existing state/schema/finite/frozen/metadata/replay checks and needs no training-producer changes.
findings.required_regression: Reject extra state keys including a NaN extra tensor, wrong dtype, and false selection/test/parameter metadata in latest, while accepting the producer's ordinary latest copy.

findings.title: Impossible counts in discarded-epoch history are accepted as verified history
findings.problem: History checks sets, KEEP+replacement total, finite values and supervised count, then derives rank, but does not validate count types/ranges or population bounds. Epochs1..7 have no retained checkpoint unless one is best, so their metrics never reach compare_metrics. A nonqualifying early row with impossible counts passes all later verification.

independent_reproduction.modified_row: Epoch1 holdout, leaving all retained checkpoint rows and artifacts unchanged.

findings.impact: The accepted history can contain negative action/harm counts or more lost recoveries than lost states. Finite values and an arithmetic sum do not establish valid metric populations. Rank-selection history depends on these unchecked rows.
findings.minimal_required_fix: Require the expected metric schema, integer count fields and nonnegative bounds in every history row. Compare sequence/reliable/lost/supervised populations with the accepted data, bound harm by reliable_sets, recovery by lost_sets, replacements/unknown selections by their populations, and require finite durations. For early discarded epochs, explicitly retain the limit that structural consistency cannot independently recompute their actual predictions.
findings.required_regression: Reject the epoch1 counterexample, fractional/negative counts and recovery above lost population before ranking, even when the row is nonqualifying and has no retained checkpoint.
